headline: India Raises Key Rate to 5.5% in First Hike Since 2023
seoDescription: India's central bank raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and shifted to calibrated tightening as inflation risks broadened.
deck: The Reserve Bank of India lifted its repo rate by 25 basis points and ruled out near-term cuts as energy and food-price pressures widened.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India raised its policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on October 7, its first increase since February 2023. The six-member Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously for the increase.

The standing deposit facility rate moved to 5.25%, while the marginal standing facility rate and bank rate rose to 5.75%. The committee also shifted its policy stance from neutral to calibrated tightening.

sections.heading: Confirmed and projected
paragraphs: The rate decision and policy stance are confirmed in the RBI's official resolution and were independently reported by Reuters and The Indian Express.

The RBI projected 7.1% real GDP growth and 5.2% consumer inflation for fiscal 2026-27. Those figures are forecasts, not realized outcomes. Two committee members preferred retaining a neutral stance even though the rate vote itself was unanimous.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: India is a major Asian economy and trading partner. A tighter policy cycle can influence regional capital flows, currencies, borrowing costs and commodity demand. For the Philippines, the signal matters as domestic inflation and high energy prices also constrain household budgets and central-bank policy choices.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch India's inflation data, oil prices and the October 21 publication of the committee minutes. The RBI said future action could be another increase or a pause, depending on actual inflation and growth.
